Test these items: where 0..* root-level FHIRPath constraints, every where constraint must evaluate true for resource inclusion, false, empty, and null filter results exclude rows as specified, non-boolean where results are rejected or surfaced as spec errors, where.description 0..1 human-readable text retention, constant references and complex FHIRPath expressions inside where clauses, filter SQL generation preserves intended root-resource scope. For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2.0.0 ViewDefinition.where.path is 1..1 string; ViewDefinition.where.description is 0..1 string; SQL-on-FHIR where filters require every FHIRPath constraint to evaluate true; FHIR JSON properties cannot be null.
issues.evidence: .temp/qa/sof_vd09_skeptic_probe.py reproduced that ViewDefinition(resource="Patient", select=[...], where=[{"description": None}]).to_dict() emits {"where": [{"description": None}]} instead of rejecting the malformed root where object. parse_view_definition() and SQLGenerator.generate() reject the same shape, so the official JSON serializer boundary is inconsistent.
issues.root_cause: Root ViewDefinition.to_dict() copied self.where entries without the shared validate_where_conditions() boundary used by parser, Select.to_dict(), and SQLGenerator.generate().
issues.resolution: ViewDefinition.to_dict() now rejects where=None and validates/non-empty root where through validate_where_conditions(), preserving valid description metadata and rejecting missing path or null/non-string description.
